name: VerusBridge duplicate-proof-root parser divergence
summary: NotarizationSerializer used the last Verus proof-root entry when duplicate system IDs were present, while Verus consensus kept the first. Two signed notarizations therefore installed and confirmed an attacker-chosen root that authorized a later unbacked import.
notes: The Delegator's contracts[9] slot changed to NotarizationSerializer 0x95b8005c4d9fe80f0aee5b7adce53766080600fb. Exhaustive review of all pre-incident upgrade calls found no later write to this module slot.

The failure-finalizing notarization is anchored 252 seconds before the payout transaction. The drain receipt and call trace establish the exact eight asset quantities; the USD total uses incident-time DefiLlama prices for ETH, tBTC, MKR and scrvUSD and par for DAI, USDC, USDT and EURC.

The incident is anchored to the second poisoned notarization, which finalized the attacker-controlled root. The later transaction 0xa1f1e65c1cea4dba4ae439cd4dcdba6cc2dbda0ed1228e61f29ae9c9324eb099 consumed that root and paid the loss but did not execute the defective parser.
The defect-executing artifact is the NotarizationSerializer module selected in contracts[9], not the SubmitImports or VerusProof modules used by the later payout.
